prose_updates.related_work: Lee and Gu (2026) study binary latent coordinates with arbitrary observed variables on nondegenerate separable metric spaces under their standing BLCM assumptions, including faithfulness.  The reduced-assumption binary-response rank class used here is a strengthening proved directly; the published Theorem 1 transfers only on its faithful intersection.  The binary-response identification comparator is a subclass of their Theorem 2 domain.  For \(q\ge3\), the present result is a categorical-latent analogue with an additional local Gram-rank certificate, not an inclusion transfer.  Chen et al. (2025) obtain mixed-type recovery through completeness and two sufficient measurements.  Their unchanged published class and the full heterogeneous finite-observed certified class are incomparable: the first noncontainment is witnessed by the equal-alphabet dense ternary member, whose observed and latent supports both have size three and therefore fail Chen et al.'s strict larger-support requirement, while the reverse noncontainment is witnessed by Chen-class members with continuous measurements, which cannot belong to the finite-observed certified class.  The support-cardinality argument is confined to the equal-alphabet witness; heterogeneous certified members may overlap Chen's class without altering either noncontainment.  Allman, Matias, and Rhodes (2009) give generic latent-class uniqueness under Kruskal inequalities; here certified full-rank row minors and third-view separation yield exact uniqueness, after which the equality lattice supplies the missing coordinate product, measurement adjacency, and latent MEC.  Gu (2026) gives constructive unfolding queries under pure-item conditions, and Kivva et al. (2021) recover structure from a mixture oracle; \(A_q\) instead enumerates exact row minors, coordinate partitions, nonnegative normalized measurement tables, and latent DAGs directly from \(P_X\).  Gu and Xu (2021) and Gu et al. (2018) motivate the software consumer and its still-open calibrated empirical layer.
